summary.intent: Execute a handed-off multi-lane sync-pass wave: run three parallel agent lanes to fix four GitHub issues (#2016, #2021, #1956, #2017) in the cipher-box engine/desktop code, review each PR, request CodeRabbit reviews, merge, and then write up the resulting doc/ADR updates.
summary.outcome: All three PRs (2059, 2060, 2063) were merged, closing all four issues; post-merge checks on main stayed green throughout (2800 engine tests passing at final commit be3d181da). Repo cleanup removed 37 stale placeholder branches and worktrees, and a follow-up ADR 0054 plus blueprint/CONTEXT doc updates were drafted and pushed as a docs PR.

repo: The retire ledger entry format is now versioned (0x02 prefix) with an origin, node id, owed/manifest byte counts, and a target-set of CID+pinnedBytes pairs, while legacy 68-byte entries still decode for backward compatibility.

An acknowledged-sequence mark stored under key prefix cbx/ra/<owner>/<node>, sealed via the RetireLedger custody, now prevents a dropped/discarded version from resurfacing at a sequence a later record already confirmed.

Staleness rung reads (status()/snapshot()) previously had a side-effect gap: an event was only sent when the rung differed from the last emitted event, not the last read, so a read mid-pass could get stuck showing 'reconciling' after the pass converged; fixed via SyncStatus::observe recording every read.

refresh_deadline (engine) and RECORD_TIMEOUT_MS (packages/client/src/seams/scheduler.ts) are two independently hard-coded 30s values that should reference each other; PR 2060 added comments linking them but did not unify them.
Desktop wake/reconnect detection keys IPv6 addresses by their /64 prefix so daily-rotating temporary addresses don't spuriously trigger a forced sync pass.

The cut-epoch floor check (refuse_below_cut_floor / check_publishable) previously existed in three independent hand-written copies across net/rotation.rs and sync/drain.rs with inconsistent error verdicts; consolidated behind one gate helper.
AGENTS.md enforces a 'no happy-path narration' comment rule — comments must not restate control flow or list callers, only capture non-obvious constraints.

code.finding: run_past_deadline hand-rolled a poll_fn race duplicating the existing `within` combinator (record_plane.rs:153); simplification/reuse reviews recommended replacing it with `within(...).await` pattern.
staleness_now took borrow_mut on every read just to write `reported`, duplicating classify logic also in report_rung (line ~10849); consolidated into SyncStatus::observe.

live_owing_record's Edit-base comparison only checked head CID equality, allowing a dropped version to resurface if a later record reused the same sequence number (acked-but-unconfirmed PUT race) — real MEDIUM loss path found by crypto-privacy review, fixed by adding a durable acknowledged-sequence mark.
refuse_below_cut_floor re-implemented cipherbox_core::seal::refuse_stale_cut_epoch by hand instead of reusing the gate's existing helper (gate/adoption.rs:367).
Removed the Wake enum/list-of-moments design in favor of a single woke(last, next) -> bool decision function, capping sampler passes to one per sample.

workflow: Multi-lane pattern: launch N background Agent lanes for independent issues, each spawning its own nested review sub-agents (simplification/reuse/efficiency/altitude, security, crypto-privacy, code-review); the orchestrator holds partial nested-review notifications until all arrive, then forwards them together with explicit accept/reject decisions.

A completed background agent's task-notification can fire multiple times (e.g. after a simplify pass with uncommitted work, then again after security review) — must inspect worktree/PR state and SendMessage to resume with the remaining steps each time, since the agent stops itself with no live children rather than finishing the whole pipeline in one run.

CodeRabbit review requests are rate/slot-limited; when a background Bash tool call would exceed its 10-minute cap waiting for a slot, relaunch the wait as a detached process or a Monitor watcher instead.

When git worktrees are removed by agents, leftover local branches (merged into main) accumulate and should be pruned in bulk, but any unmerged branch must be diffed against main before deletion to confirm its content already landed (e.g. via squash-merge) before removing it.

After each PR merge: fast-forward local main, remove the corresponding worktree, and run a post-merge check (clippy + full engine test suite) under a Monitor before considering the wave step complete.
Reviewing agent-authored PRs personally (reading diff stats, source diff, CodeRabbit comments) before spending a CodeRabbit review slot is part of this workflow's gating.

friction: An Opus agent (Lane A) died mid-task due to hitting the session rate limit (reset at 8:20pm Europe/Berlin), losing ~3 hours of wall-clock time until reset before it could be resumed.
Lane C's simplify agent stopped twice with uncommitted work and no PR/report, requiring manual inspection and resumption via SendMessage each time.
Background Bash tool calls have a 10-minute cap that can't cover an 11+ minute CodeRabbit slot wait, requiring workaround via detached process/Monitor.
One 'Repo / Tracker Refs' CI check reported success while its status still read in-progress, an inconsistency that had to be manually reconciled rather than trusted at face value.
37 stale placeholder branches from previously removed agent worktrees had accumulated in the repo, requiring manual audit and cleanup.
open_items: ADR 0047 amendment for two new durable storage shapes (versioned retire-ledger entry grammar, and the acknowledged-sequence mark under cbx/ra/) — drafted as ADR 0054 and pushed as a docs PR, but not yet reviewed/merged.
blueprint/engine.md 'Staleness ladder' section needs a line stating Reconciling lasts at most one refresh_deadline — addressed in the same docs PR pending review.
CONTEXT.md 'Manual refresh' section needs to name the overdue failure as a third way a refresh can end — addressed in the same docs PR pending review.
Issue #2065 filed as follow-up: dropped version whose staged root is already gone means nothing journals its rows; candidate design is a charge-time journal instead of release-time.
The drain signs a scope root without acquiring the write-epoch lease that check_publishable's doc says the floor read depends on — flagged as an open design question in the PR body, not resolved.
T3 worktree on the staging-soak branch (zero commits ahead of main) was intentionally left alone since another Code thread owns it.
Scheduler seam has no timer-cancel/AbortSignal method, so web setTimeout timers from run_past_deadline/file_forced_pass are not cleared early (accepted as minor efficiency residual, not fixed).
